key_insight: Annealing a thermally sprayed Ni-based coating at 800°C for 1 h produced a refined three-phase microstructure and reduced wear rate by 89%.
engineering_relevance: Controlled crystallization offers a route to wear-resistant coatings that combine ductile crack resistance with hard, load-bearing intermetallic phases.
method: Thermally spray a designed Ni–Cr–Nb–P–B–Si amorphous alloy powder.
Anneal at 800°C for 1 h to transform the metastable phase into Ni-based solid solution, Ni₃P, and NbNi₃.
Evaluate microstructure, friction, wear rate, and worn-surface damage.
evidence_signal: Relative to the as-sprayed coating, annealing reduced intersplat density by 51%, coefficient of friction by 21%, and wear rate by 89%, with no observed worn-surface spallation, delamination, or cracking.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear-test conditions or substrate compatibility with the 800°C treatment, limiting assessment of service applicability.
paper_title: Enhanced Wear Resistance of Fine-Grained Ni-Based Coating via Annealing-Induced Phase Transformation
